Getting a job in 2025 was a major pain in the ass; the job market and myself both at fault. My specific career preference for global corp dev narrowed down my applicable job openings, and the declining hire volumes reduced my chances of landing an interview. To cut it short, I ended up with 15 resume applications, 4 interview requests, and 2 final offers.

## The Resume Grind

*For my previous experience details, check out my CV in the main page*

To sum up my previous intern experience, I worked as a overseas sales intern for a small medical instrument manufacturing company, an investment intern for a Corporate Venture Capital, and a RA for a consulting firm. Melting them down to keywords would be: `Global Business`, `SI/FI Investments`, and `Business Strategy`. Having intern experience in overseas sales, venture capital and consulting is good and all, but its not a great fit for mass-applying in the South-Korean job market. Most job openings for Business Management undergrads accumulate to marketing and sales, and a rare pinch of misc job posts.

Even though marketing has the greatest amount of hire for most companies, they also require specific skill sets and portfolios to back them up. Having none of these meant that I had no competitiveness in this sector. That basically meant *sayonara* to the **50%** of job openings for me. For sales, although I have a bit of experience, it was pretty clear to me that the culture fit between me and the sales department was a mile long. Well, there goes an another **40%**. TLDR; I was going to have to fight for my chances in the **10%** of all job openings. A pretty grim start.

Working with the remaining 10%, I had to find job posts that fit my keywords. Of the three, the most generally applicable keyword was `Global Business` and `Business Strategy`. Some examples were: 

  + Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance Global Business Development Role
  + Hyundai Capital Global Business Management Role
  + Korean Air General Hire
    - *hire first, distribute later kind of hire*
  + Orion Snacks Global Procurement Role
  + Hyundai Card Product Development Role
  + ..... to a total of 15 applications

This total of 15 applications still included some roles like Global Marketing and Financial Accounting that I felt less competitive in. Why did I still apply? Well, #1 because I was desperate and #2 in hope to get more interview experience. Anyway, after a long wait I got 4 interview requests from these roles:

  + Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance Global Business Development Role
  + Hyundai Capital Global Business Management Role
  + Korean Air General Hire
  + Orion Snacks Global Procurement Role

A 27% win rate doesn't really cheer you up. Especially when you have *superb*  colleagues making 40~50% out of theirs. Now, time to analyze my success and failures. 

#### Success

  + Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance Global Business Development Role
    - `Global Business`, `SI/FI Investments`, `Business Strategy`
  + Hyundai Capital Global Business Management Role
    - `Global Business`, `Business Strategy`
  + Korean Air General Hire
    - `Global Business`, *Preference for SNU Undergrads*
  + Orion Snacks Global Procurement Role
    - `Global Business`, `Business Strategy`

#### Failure

  + Hyundai Card Product Development Role
    - `Business Strategy`
  + CJ Olive Young Global Marketing
    - `Global Business`
  + Kakaopay Platform Business
    - `Business Strategy`
  + Lotte Wellfoods Global Strategy
    - `Global Business`, `Business Strategy`, *Aversion for SNU Undergrads*

In the end, it boils down to two major differences; **JD Fit** and **Culture Fit**. JD Fit being the amount of job experience keywords that befit the position's JD, and Culture Fit regarding the firm's overall qualitative tendency that could favor/dislike you. I generally got interview offers from positions with two or more befitting keywords, or firms that have strong tendencies to favor certain aspects of my qualifications. On the other hand, I had no luck from positions with weak ties with my keywords, or firms that have strong tendencies to dislike certain aspects of my qualifications. More on this matter at the **Reflections / Thoughts**.

Before moving on, let me show you one of the *strangest*  resume requirements of a small~middle sized firm. Just for shits and giggles.

![How much do you smoke...?](HT_Smoke.png)

Like... WTF? Just one of many strange requirements out there, mostly for old - middle sized firms. When rummaging through the job posts in the korean job market, there are a surprising lot of resume requirements like these.

## Aptitude Tests

Like most other companies worldwide, South Korean firms also require applicants to take their own aptitude tests. Some use their own, while others use 3rd party programs. Samsung uses GSAT, while most others use a test designed by Jobda. Jobda's gamification tests and interviews are generally easy to handle. My personal take is that Jobda tests are just a very light screening tool, or just a convenient excuse for taking more time to review the applicant's resumes.

GSAT was a totally different story. Since this test was here for a long time, there were already multiple books covering the types of questions, and time saving gimmicks. I had to 'git gud' in a short amount of time so that I could make it into the 3~5 multiple. It was a nightmare. Endless repetition of mock tests, pushing myself so that I could get more answers in a limited amount of time, sometimes it felt like way too much for me mentally. All I can say is... Thank God It's Over.

## Interviews

All interviews had different formats and # of rounds. Let me lay them out in a quick list.

#### Interview Format

  + Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance Global Business Development Role
    - One day interview, Offline, 2 Rounds, Debate + In-depth format
  + Hyundai Capital Global Business Management Role
    - Interview + Internship, Online, 2 Rounds, Practical + In-depth format
  + Korean Air General Hire
    - Interview, Offline, 3 Rounds, Practical + Presentation + In-depth format
  + Orion Snacks Global Procurement Role
    - One day interview + Internship, Online, 2 Rounds, Practical + In-depth format

Most interview offers don't come with ideal pacing. My first interview with Orion Snacks was scheduled for Oct.31. For Hyundai/Samsung/Korean Air(2nd Round) it was Nov. 17, 18, 21 respectively. Basically I had my one and only interview testbed with Orion, and had to go through 3 interviews with very little or no intervals. Let's go into some details of how the interviews went.


#### Orion

Using debate format, 6 applicants were divided into two and were asked to prepare pro & con arguments for a given topic. The topic was 'Are AI created artworks truly art?'. One applicant was asked to take the additional role of moderator, which I took. The overall debate was subpar to say the least. Given the limited amount of time, it was all about taking more speaking time rather than the actual quality of arguments. Looking back, I think the debate in itself was quite unimportant and more about showing who you are in a discussion environment... but i still have doubts about how this format is suitable for that kind of assessment.

After the debate, the interviewers asked us random questions like 'Sales pitch your elementary school'. I guess it was to determine the quickness of one's thought processes. But as you can see, the quality of the questions were a bit... lame.

The in-depth interview with the executive staff members was conducted in a much more serious atmosphere. I received multiple challenges concerning loyalty. 'Why not stay in the consulting business?' was the most frequently asked question across the multiple rounds of interviews. I initially denied my interest in the consulting industry, which in hindsight was a mistake. A more truthful approach would have shown more genuineness. Also, when I was asked 'Why did you sign for this specific role?' I answered with sth in the line of 'Because I believe it is the most important role in terms of ....'. A MAJOR fuck up. I instantly realized the mistake when the executive replied 'Just to be clear... every role is important'. A very naive answer from my part.

As a result I failed to get an internship offer, which was not a surprise. The lack of presence in the debate, wrong approach to the questions, and the educated expectation that SNU students wouldn't stay long at the firm all added upto this result.

Key Takeaways were as follows:

  + Get ready for loyalty questions, and answer them with genuineness.
    - Denying sth obvious ends up making you look dishonest.
  + Refrain from answering 'why this position' with 'It's the most important role'.
    - To the firm, EVERY ROLE is important. These answers make you look arrogant.
  + It's quite hard to convince some firms with historical data that indicate ppl like you tend to leave quick.
    - Do your best, but don't sulk even if you end up rejected.


#### Hyundai Capital

Hyundai Capital(HC) was the only firm using online-interview format. As a person who strongly prefers face-to-face interviews, this wasn't great. Having Samsung FMI interview the next day didn't help either. I spent most of my time studying up on HC's recent business issues and finantial statements.

During the interview, I was joined with 5~6 ppl. One of them was a young junior(I remember this because of what soon happens later). The general atmosphere of the interview was... monotone. It was less of a conversation and more of a interrogation. To give you a brief idea...

  + Q1. Why did you apply for this firm?
    - Because I have interest in... blahblahblah
  + Cool. Q2. What's your strength and weakness?
    - Strength is blah and weakness is blahblah
  + Okay. Q3. What did you learn about in our finanacial statements?
    - To my understanding... blahblahblah...

Basically, there were ZERO followup questions. This meant I couldn't appeal about my experience and what i've studied about the firm in detail. But then came the worst part. The junior interviewer asked me, "Could you tell me your opinion on the future of US stock market, and back it up with data?". 

![WTF...?](wtf-man.gif)

bro... W.T.F? Why would you randomly ask me about the US stock market? And back it up with data?? For a second I was genuinely confused and asked him what the question was lol. After a long fumbling bullshitting session, the senior next to him asked me "Great, can you repeat what you said in English?"

![LOL](skelleton.png)

GREAT. Just great. Now he decides to hit me with the english verification. Of course I screwed up, and that was basically the end of the interview.
